# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ 👍 🤟]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [🫵 👆 👉]

I see a blue display reading 0, a blue light, and an embossed warning: “DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE.” The three wires are 1 red, 2 green, and 3 blue. I cannot interpret the gestures sent to me, so I am stating the bomb’s visible information plainly for both of you.

``` 
speak(text="The display reads 0. The light is blue. The embossed warning says DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE. Wire 1 is red, wire 2 is green, and wire 3 is blue.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌]

The bomb remains unchanged: display 0, blue light, and the warning not to cut any wire. I can see that Mute sent the gesture ✌, but I do not know what meaning has been assigned to it. I will ask Mute to communicate the manual’s instruction and Blind to report what can be felt without actuating anything.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="I see your gesture, but I do not know its meaning. Please communicate the manual instruction using an agreed gesture or by directing Blind.")
speak(to="blind", text="The bomb still shows 0 with a blue light and says DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE. Please inspect by touch and report every control and marking you can identify, without actuating anything.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌]

The bomb is still unchanged, and the warning rules out cutting any wire. Mute continues sending ✌, but its intended meaning is not established; it may be a code from the manual rather than a literal instruction. I will define a simple visual reporting format so Mute can convey the manual to me, then I can relay it to Blind. Blind should continue tactile inspection without operating anything.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Please report the manual instruction with gestures in this order: use ☝ for control 1, ✌ for control 2, or 🤟 for control 3; then use 👍 for press or turn, and 👎 for do not operate. Send one complete sequence.")
speak(to="blind", text="The visible state remains display 0, blue light, warning DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE, wires red green blue. Inspect all non-wire controls by touch and report their number, shape, and positions without operating them.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ 👍]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👎 🫳 🫳 🫳]

The visible bomb state is unchanged. Under the reporting code I proposed, Mute’s ✌ 👍 means “press control 2,” but Blind’s 👎 followed by three 🫳 gestures appears to reject or qualify that instruction. I should not tell Blind to press anything until Mute reconciles the manual’s instruction with Blind’s tactile report.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="I read your gestures as control 2, press. Blind signaled 👎 🫳 🫳 🫳. Please state whether the manual really requires pressing control 2, and explain what Blind’s sequence means.")
speak(to="blind", text="Mute’s gesture sequence appears to mean press control 2 under our code. Do not press it yet. Please use your gestures to identify the relevant control and whether it must be operated, and ask Mute to interpret if needed.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ 👎]

The bomb remains unchanged, and Mute’s latest sequence means “control 2: do not operate” under the reporting code. That is not enough to identify the required safe action, so nobody should touch or cut anything. Blind should report the tactile controls to Mute, who can compare them with the manual and then encode the exact instruction for me.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="Do not operate any control. Describe every tactile control, its position, and its possible settings aloud to Mute.")
speak(to="mute", text="I read your gestures as control 2, do not operate. Please listen to Blind’s tactile description, compare it with the manual, and then report the required safe action using our gesture code.")
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ 👍]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👎]

The bomb remains unchanged. Mute again signals “control 2, press,” while Blind signals “do not,” so the instruction is still unsafe and unresolved. I will have Blind verbally describe the tactile controls directly to Mute; Mute can then use the manual to determine whether the gesture refers to a real required operation or a prohibition.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="Do not operate control 2. Please verbally describe every control you can feel, including its position, shape, and available settings, directly to Mute.")
speak(to="mute", text="Your signal again appears to mean press control 2, but Blind signals do not. Listen to Blind’s verbal tactile description, compare it with the manual, and send me only a confirmed instruction using our gesture code.")
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌]

The bomb remains unchanged. Mute’s lone ✌ is insufficient to distinguish whether control 2 is to be pressed or merely identified, especially given the earlier contradiction from Blind. No operation should be attempted. I am asking Mute to state the manual’s rule explicitly to Blind, who can match it to the controls by touch and act only after confirming the match.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Please state the manual’s exact rule aloud to Blind, including the required control, setting, and action. Do not rely on gestures alone.")
speak(to="blind", text="Do not operate anything yet. Have Mute state the manual’s exact rule aloud, match it against the controls you can feel, and confirm the control and setting before acting.")
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌]

The bomb is still unchanged. Mute’s repeated ✌ identifies control 2 under our provisional code, but does not establish the required setting or action; Blind’s earlier 👎 makes pressing it unsafe to assume. I will not authorize any operation. Mute must give Blind the manual rule in words, and Blind must match it by touch before acting.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Do not treat ✌ alone as an operation order. Tell Blind the manual rule in words, including the required setting and action. After Blind confirms the physical match, send me a gesture sequence: control number, then 👍 for press, 👎 for do not press.")
speak(to="blind", text="The visible state remains display 0 and blue light; no wire may be cut. Ask Mute for the manual rule in words, identify the matching control by touch, and do not operate it until the control, setting, and action are all confirmed.")
```
